ai.title: Add Reddit funnel and attribution analytics events
ai.summary: Added six new analytics events to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`: `FREEBUFF_ATTRIBUTED` for UTM/ad-click super-properties, and five `FREEBUFF_REDDIT_FUNNEL_*` events covering CLI install, login, sign-up, first prompt, and gravity ad click. These track acquisition attribution and Reddit ad funnel conversion in PostHog, filterable by `utm_source` and `reddit_click_id`. Scope limited to the shared constants file; no other packages or surfaces modified. Events are enum members only; actual emission logic is not included in this diff.

eli5.text: The assistant can now be tracked when it comes from a Reddit ad. If you clicked a Reddit ad to install or sign up for the assistant, the team now records six specific steps in that journey, like when you first run it, log in, sign up, send your first message, or click the gravity ad again, plus one event that captures which ad or link originally brought you there. Nothing looks different to you on screen; this just sets up the named steps so the team can later build the parts of the product that actually report when those steps happen.

facts: GLM 5.2 is a referral reward, not a freely-pickable model, so it's surfaced by the separate FreebuffReferralBanner rather than this grid.

GLM 5.2 referral-reward session pool. Distinct from the premium daily pool: GLM sessions reset weekly (Pacific) and the per-user limit is the caller's GLM referral score, capped at FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_REFERRAL_CAP.
Max number of qualified referrals that count toward GLM sessions, i.e. the most 1-hour GLM sessions a user can earn per week.
GLM sessions are exactly one hour of wall-clock time, regardless of the global free-session length, so the "1 hour per referral per week" promise is exact.

No data-collection warning: served by Fireworks (no provider-side training), and omitting it keeps GLM out of FREEBUFF_TRACED_MODEL_IDS. `premium` drives the "Premium" badge styling in the picker; GLM's real gate is its weekly referral-session pool, not the daily premium pool.

ai.title: GLM 5.2 referral sessions and banner
ai.summary: GLM 5.2 added as referral reward via base2-free-glm.ts and code-reviewer-glm.ts. Excluded from model picker in freebuff-model-selector.tsx, surfaced in new freebuff-referral-banner.tsx. Weekly session pool distinct from premium daily, capped by FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_REFERRAL_CAP. Sessions exactly one hour, served by Fireworks, omitted from FREEBUFF_TRACED_MODEL_IDS.

eli5.text: If you use the free assistant, a new model is now available to you, but only as a thank-you gift for getting friends to sign up: each friend you refer earns you one hour of access to this newer model each week. You'll see a small banner on the waiting screen that tells you whether you've unlocked it yet and, if you have, how many hours you still have left this week, along with a button to copy your personal referral link to share with friends. The regular model picker no longer shows this option at all, because it's meant to be earned through referrals rather than chosen directly.

facts: Identify first so the login event is attributed to the real user id and the pre-login anonymous history is aliased in.

Returning users restore an existing session instead of going through the login modal, so `cli.login` would otherwise never fire for them, making them look like a login-step drop-off in the funnel even though they're authenticated. Emit it here too, tagged by `via`.
Identify first (aliases the pre-login anonymous history to the real user id) so the login event below is attributed to the user.

This flow runs outside the TUI and exits immediately, so the React-based login tracking never runs. Identify + track here (tagged `via`) so these logins aren't missing from the funnel, then flush before exiting since process.exit would otherwise drop the buffered PostHog events.
Persisting it to the config dir means all of a user's pre-login launches collapse to a single person that aliases cleanly into their account.
entries.title: CLI update: use-auth-state

ai.title: Persistent anonymous analytics id and cli.login on session restore
ai.summary: Anonymous PostHog id now persists to config dir via cli/src/utils/anonymous-id.ts, replacing per-process generateAnonymousId in cli/src/utils/analytics.ts. Pre-login launches collapse to one person that aliases cleanly into the account. cli.login now fires on session restore (via='session_restore') in cli/src/hooks/use-auth-state.ts and on plain login (via='plain_command') in cli/src/login/plain-login.ts, with flushAnalytics before process.exit. getConfigDir moved to cli/src/utils/config-dir.ts to break an import cycle; auth.ts re-exports it as a wrapper so existing spyOn(authModule, 'getConfigDir') tests keep working.

eli5.text: When you use the CodeBuff CLI tool, it now assigns you the same anonymous tracking ID every time you launch it before you log in, instead of creating a brand-new ID with each launch. This means all your pre-login activity (like opening the app multiple times) gets grouped together under one identity, rather than appearing as separate individual sessions that look like people dropping off before logging in. The system then properly records your login when you sign in through the web flow or when your existing session is restored automatically, so your pre-login and post-login activity is correctly linked to your actual account. If you're a developer looking at the analytics, you'll now see the complete user journey from first launch through login as one continuous activity instead of

facts: Referrals are a full-tier-only perk: limited users never earn GLM sessions, so the whole banner is hidden for them. The server already omits the `referral` block for non-full tiers; this is a belt-and-suspenders guard.
The inviter's display name (`user.name`), used to personalize the invite landing page ("X invited you to try Freebuff!"). Null when the user has no name set.
entries.title: CLI update: freebuff-referral-banner

ai.title: Referral banner now links to /get-started with referrer name
ai.summary: The referral share link now points at the /get-started CLI install walkthrough instead of the bare landing page, passing the inviter's display name as an optional ?referrer= query parameter so the page can greet the friend with "X invited you to try Freebuff!", per the referrerName field newly added to FreebuffReferralInfo. freebuff-referral-banner.tsx introduces a CopyInviteLinkButton that wraps copyTextToClipboard and flips to a 'Copied!' confirmation for COPIED_RESET_DELAY_MS milliseconds, replacing the previous CopyButton usage. The FreebuffReferralBanner is also reordered to render after the streak line in the waiting-room landing layout, keeping it visually anchored to the model picker.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/components/freebuff-referral-banner.tsx, referralLink now takes a referrerName argument and builds a /get-started link with ?ref= and optional ?referrer=, and a new CopyInviteLinkButton component replaces CopyButton for clipboard feedback. In common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts, FreebuffReferralInfo gains a referrerName: string | null field. In cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx, the FreebuffReferralBanner render slot is moved to the bottom of the landing picker column
ai.migration: No action required; existing referral links continue to work and the new referrer personalization is applied automatically.

changes.what: Reworked referral link generation and clipboard button to target /get-started with an optional referrer name parameter, adding a CopyInviteLinkButton with copied-state feedback.
Added referrerName: string | null to FreebuffReferralInfo, sourced from user.name, for landing-page personalization.
Moved the FreebuffReferralBanner render slot below the streak row in the landing picker column.
